how: Each time your operative levels up you get materials and pick one passive skill from a skill tree.
The tree is different for every player and reshuffles with each new Personal Timeline, so there's no fixed best order. Pick by goal instead.
Skills stack with your body sleeve and chronogenes. Check Modified Stats on the Characteristics screen after each pick; some bonuses stack less than 1:1.

priorities.pick: Healing, armor or damage resistance first, then movement so you can disengage.
Carrying capacity first, then anything that makes extraction safer.
Weapon handling first, with one escape or movement skill so you can reset fights.
One combat, one survival and one utility skill before specializing.

skills.agency: The Agency investigations Vitality and Chronogene Theory (Monolith Beta) and Strength and Perception (Delta) are cheap and build on your characteristics. Grab them as soon as they unlock.

how: You have 4 chronogene slots on the Characteristics screen. Swap them between raids.
Most come in Tier I, II and III (Common, Uncommon, Rare). Ability chronogenes are Rare with a single tier.
You can own only one chronogene of each type at a time.
Tier III has 10 charges. Dying burns charges; at 0 it drops to Tier II. Overcharged ones (Overunstable) burn 1–2 per death.
Tier III synthesis: 20 Active Matter + 3 random Tier II chronogenes, instant, random result. Mixed inputs favor the majority color.
Other chronogenes come from the Replicator using creature remains (Distorted, Dendroid, Shy Girl, Devourer…). Epsilon unlocks Tier III synthesis.
Equipped chronogenes are discarded when you start a new Personal Timeline. Unequip the good ones first.

tiered.name: Active Matter Gathering
tiered.detail: Collect Active Matter faster, so you spend less time exposed at nests and deposits.

tiered.name: Breath Control
tiered.detail: Hold your breath longer while aiming down sights for steadier long shots.

tiered.name: Bulletproof
tiered.detail: Reduces damage you take from bullets.

tiered.name: Carrying Capacity
tiered.detail: Cuts the movement and stamina penalty from heavy loads, so you can carry more loot.

tiered.name: Cold-blooded
tiered.detail: Lowers your body temperature build-up; helps in hot zones and fire.

tiered.name: Endurance
tiered.what: Pulse escalation and stamina drain (fatigue threshold +3 / +5 / +7)
tiered.detail: Your pulse climbs slower and stamina drains slower, and you can push harder before fatigue (+3/+5/+7 fatigue threshold).

tiered.name: Examination
tiered.detail: Identify unknown items faster when searching containers and bodies.

tiered.name: Fine Motor Skills
tiered.what: Reload, mag stuffing and healing-item speed
tiered.detail: Faster reloading, magazine loading and healing-item use.

tiered.name: Fire Resistance
tiered.detail: Reduces fire damage from Molotovs, Scorch, fireballs and burning ground.

tiered.name: Heal Efficiency
tiered.detail: Medkits and healing items restore more health.

tiered.name: Hit Stability
tiered.what: View and aim shake when hit
tiered.detail: Less screen shake, aim shake and hand stamina loss when you get hit.

tiered.name: Jump
tiered.detail: Jump higher and take a little less fall damage (+3/+5/+7%).

tiered.name: Melee
tiered.detail: More melee damage.

tiered.name: Overflow Healing
tiered.what: Extra healing spread to all body parts
tiered.detail: Part of each healing ampule also heals your other body parts.

tiered.name: Pain Shock
tiered.detail: Recover from pain shock faster after heavy hits.

tiered.name: Resilience
tiered.detail: Reduces melee damage you take from monsters and players.

tiered.name: Serenity
tiered.detail: Stamina and pulse recover faster, and activity raises your heart rate less.

tiered.name: Speed
tiered.detail: Move faster at all times.

tiered.name: Sprint
tiered.detail: Sprint faster.

tiered.name: Sprint Duration
tiered.detail: Sprint for longer before running out of stamina.

tiered.name: Steady Hand
tiered.detail: Your arms tire slower while aiming, so you can hold aim longer.

abilities.name: Active Matter Locator
abilities.what: Shows the direction of nearby Active Matter

abilities.name: Berserk
abilities.what: High heart rate boosts melee damage

abilities.name: Calming Effect
abilities.what: Healing items also lower your heart rate

abilities.name: Limb Regeneration
abilities.what: Critically injured limbs slowly recover to pain-free

abilities.name: Monster Detector
abilities.what: Shows the direction of nearby monsters

abilities.name: Motion Detector
abilities.what: Shows where movement was recently detected

abilities.name: Night Owl
abilities.what: Slightly better vision in the dark

abilities.name: Observation
abilities.what: Highlights nearby lootable containers and items

abilities.name: Parkour
abilities.what: Pull up on ledges, grab edges mid-air, push off walls

abilities.name: Sharp Memory
abilities.what: Always know your magazine round count

abilities.name: Tenacity
abilities.what: Once per raid, lethal damage puts you in shock instead of killing you (not headshots)

abilities.name: Trap Sense
abilities.what: Shows the direction of nearby traps

remains.note: Also used for the Underground laboratory key and Bunker south entrance key.
Found under destroyed hives, not on a body.

remainsHow: Each kill can drop remains. Fuse them in the Workshop to roll a random chronogene from that creature's list; the percentages are the roll chances.
Pristine remains drop rarely and always roll the creature's signature chronogene at Tier II (90%) or Tier III (10%).
Ability chronogenes (Tenacity, Observation and the rest) don't come from normal remains. The Distorted Chronogene Study investigation unlocks a recipe for Rare chronogenes from Distorted.
Remains you don't need refine for 40 credits each (pristine ones for 120).
chrono.abilitySource: Ability chronogenes don't drop from normal monster remains. They come from Tier III random synthesis (20 Active Matter + 3 Tier II chronogenes, unlocked at Monolith Epsilon) and the Rare chronogene recipe from the Distorted Chronogene Study investigation.
chrono.noRemains: Not tied to any monster's remains. Get it from random Tier II/III synthesis.

builds.name: Survival (PvE)
builds.swap: Monster Detector or Trap Sense on maps with lots of anomalies; Fire Resistance for Park.
builds.sleeve: Beast or Rock in Isolated Raids; Knight in Open Raids; Paladin if you heal the squad.
builds.why: Tenacity is a free second life once per raid, Limb Regeneration keeps you mobile, and the other two make every medkit go further.

builds.name: Looting
builds.swap: Conduit for faster exits; Active Matter Locator on AM farming runs.
builds.why: Find containers faster, identify loot faster, carry more and grab Active Matter quicker, so you spend less time exposed.

builds.name: PvP
builds.swap: Soft Steps for ambushes; Breath Control and Steady Hand for marksman rifles; Fine Motor Skills instead of Weapon Expert if you heal mid-fight.
builds.sleeve: Ghost or Shadow to avoid being found; Knight if you plan to win the fight.
builds.why: Survive the first burst, keep your aim steady when hit, know where enemies moved, and reload faster.

builds.name: Melee
builds.swap: Serenity or Endurance to keep stamina up.
builds.sleeve: Reaper, Warlord or Mirage (big melee strength bonuses).
builds.why: Stacks melee damage with sleeves that already boost it. Good for clearing Hellhounds, Mimics and sleeping Distorted without ammo.

builds.name: Squad medic
builds.swap: Tenacity if you're the one getting focused.
builds.why: Faster revives and stronger healing keep the whole squad in the raid.

tips: Put your Tier III chronogenes in the slots that matter most for the build; they lose charges when you die, so use Tier I/II for risky experiments.
Ability chronogenes like Tenacity and Observation change how you play; take one or two over a small stat bonus.
Body sleeves stack with chronogenes and skills. Don't double up where the sleeve already covers it (e.g. Paladin already cuts body temperature 90%, so skip Cold-blooded).
After any change, check Modified Stats on the Characteristics screen.
